headline: Up to 100% basic pay hike proposed for government employees under 9th Pay Scale
summary: A high-level secretaries' committee has recommended increasing basic salaries by up to 100%, with the new scale to be rolled out in two phases.
details: A high-level secretaries' committee has recommended increasing the basic salaries of government employees in grades one to 20 by up to 100%. This recommendation is detailed in an e-book titled "180 Days of the People's Government", published by the Prime Minister's Office (PMO).

Under the sub-heading "9th Pay Scale: Great Good News for Government Employees", the publication outlines a two-phase implementation plan. Basic salary adjustments will be made in the first year, followed by house rent and other allowances in the second year.

The report notes a significant financial allocation, earmarking Tk 89,836 crore for salaries and allowances in the 2026-27 fiscal year budget. The total allocation, including pensions and gratuities, is projected to exceed Tk 1.41 lakh crore.

Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury stated that the government plans to officially announce the new pay scale this year. Discussions are ongoing, with further details to be shared once decisions are finalized.

The 9th National Pay Commission, formed on July 27, 2025, and headed by former finance secretary Zakir Ahmed Khan, submitted its report on January 21 this year. It recommended retaining the existing 20 grades and a 100-140 percent increase in total pay and allowances.

Subsequently, a 10-member secretaries' committee, led by Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Gani, was formed on April 21. This committee was tasked with recommending a comprehensive implementation strategy for the proposed new pay structure.
caption:

headline: Iranian fishermen return to Strait of Hormuz despite fears of renewed US-Iran fighting
summary: After months of conflict between Iran and the US, fishermen in Bandar Abbas are resuming their livelihood in the strategic Strait of Hormuz, facing the dual threat of war and starvation.
details: Iranian fishermen along the Strait of Hormuz have returned to sea after months of intense fighting between Iran and the United States, which forced them to halt their operations. Many, like 47-year-old Mohammad-Amin, exhausted their savings during this period, fearing their boats would be destroyed.

The conflict had a devastating impact on the local fishing community. Nearly a dozen fishermen were killed off Bandar Abbas and nearby islands, and 17 others from Sistan-Baluchistan province went missing, according to Iranian media.

Despite the ongoing tensions and the risk of renewed clashes, fishermen feel they have no choice but to return to the waters. "If we don't (go), we will die of hunger and I have three children," said Mohammad-Amin, highlighting the desperate situation.

Over 2,000 fishermen from Hormozgan province lost their equipment, and hundreds of fishing and trade boats were damaged during the fighting, which saw the Bandar Abbas waterfront repeatedly hit. The sea itself has become more dangerous, with nets frequently snagging on war wreckage.

The Strait of Hormuz remains a flashpoint, with Iran insisting on retaining control and requiring transit fees, a move opposed by Washington. While diplomats from Iran and Oman work towards an arrangement, fishermen remain largely unaware of the progress, focused solely on their ability to earn a living.

Fishermen like Hossein, 53, and Bagher Abbaszadeh, 39, express constant worry about the conflict reigniting. They emphasize that fishing is their only means of support, and they would continue to go to sea even if fighting resumed, as they have no other way to provide for their families.
